name: Frame Energy Temporal Profile
description: Profiles frame energy over time to detect abnormal energy fluctuations characteristic of AI video generation.
mechanism:
This method detects AI-generated or manipulated video by analyzing the temporal evolution of frame energy — the total signal energy per frame — which follows characteristic patterns in authentic camera-captured video:

1. **Frame Energy Extraction**: For each frame, the method computes multiple energy metrics: (a) spatial-domain energy — the sum of squared pixel intensities, (b) frequency-domain energy — the total power in the 2D DFT magnitude spectrum, partitioned into low-frequency (< 1/8 Nyquist), mid-frequency (1/8–1/2 Nyquist), and high-frequency (> 1/2 Nyquist) bands, (c) gradient energy — the sum of squared Sobel gradient magnitudes, capturing edge energy. These per-frame energy values form temporal signals E_spatial(t), E_low(t), E_mid(t), E_high(t), and E_grad(t) that characterize how the video's visual content varies over time.

2. **Natural Energy Dynamics Modeling**: Authentic camera-captured video exhibits specific energy temporal dynamics: energy changes are smooth (autocorrelation > 0.9 at lag 1), energy across frequency bands is correlated (scene changes affect all bands simultaneously), and energy fluctuations follow a 1/f spectral distribution (natural scene statistics). The method fits an autoregressive model AR(p) to each energy signal and computes the prediction error. Authentic video has low AR prediction error (< 5% of signal variance). AI-generated video often exhibits: (a) unnaturally stable energy in latent-diffusion models (energy variance < 30% of expected), (b) periodic energy oscillations from autoregressive generation, (c) decorrelated frequency-band energies when the generator processes different spatial frequencies independently.

3. **Scene-Change Energy Profiling**: At natural scene changes (cuts, transitions), frame energy exhibits characteristic transient profiles — a sharp energy change followed by stabilization within 2–3 frames as the new scene establishes. The method detects scene changes via energy step detection and validates the transient profile. AI-generated video scene transitions often show abnormal energy profiles: gradual energy ramps (instead of sharp transitions), energy oscillations after transitions (from temporal autoregressive instability), or energy levels that do not match the visual scene content (dark scenes with high-frequency energy typically associated with bright, detailed scenes).

4. **Codec-Aware Energy Analysis**: Video compression creates systematic patterns in frame energy — I-frames (keyframes) have higher energy than P/B-frames due to quantization and prediction residual structures. The method parses the video GOP (Group of Pictures) structure and normalizes energy analysis by frame type. Authentic video encoded once shows consistent I-frame to P-frame energy ratios. Tampered video that has been re-encoded (double compression) shows abnormal energy patterns within the GOP: energy ratios that change at the boundary between originally-I-frame and originally-P-frame positions. This provides an additional forensic signal for detecting post-processing of AI video.
parameters:
Energy metrics: spatial, spectral (3 bands), gradient
Frequency bands: low (< Nyquist/8), mid (Nyquist/8–Nyquist/2), high (> Nyquist/2)
AR model order: p = 5
AR prediction error threshold: > 5% indicates anomaly
Autocorrelation requirement: > 0.9 at lag 1 for natural video
Scene change detection: energy step > 3σ from running mean
GOP structure parsing: H.264/H.265 NAL unit analysis
Minimum video length: 30 frames
Analysis resolution: native resolution (no downscaling)
accuracy: 80–89% accuracy detecting AI-generated video via energy temporal profiling. AR model prediction error achieves AUC of 0.86 for distinguishing real from synthetic video. Frequency-band decorrelation is the strongest feature (AUC 0.88) for diffusion-model video. Scene change energy profiling provides F1-score of 0.83. Codec-aware analysis detects double compression with 90% accuracy. Performance is weaker for short clips (< 2 seconds).
source: Amerini, I. et al. (2019). Deepfake Video Detection through Optical Flow Based CNN. Proceedings of ICCV Workshop, 1205–1207.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated video through abnormal energy temporal dynamics. Identifying temporal manipulation (frame insertion, deletion, reordering) in forensic analysis. Double compression detection for tamper evidence. Quality assessment of video generation models.
strengths:
• Captures global temporal dynamics that are difficult for generators to control
• Multiple energy metrics provide complementary detection signals
• Codec-aware analysis detects post-processing and re-encoding
• Scene change profiling validates narrative-level temporal consistency
• Works independently of specific AI generation architecture
limitations:
• Short video clips provide insufficient temporal data for AR modeling
• Variable bitrate encoding creates energy fluctuations that may confuse the analysis
• Static or slow-moving scenes have low energy variation, reducing signal strength
• Advanced generative models with explicit temporal modeling produce more natural energy profiles
• Live streaming with adaptive bitrate changes complicates codec-aware analysis
